Before I begin, I want to comment on some notable
events. We've all watched in horror and sadness as the
violence has unfolded in the Middle East. We are reminded
during times of global violence that this region is part
of the global community. First and foremost, I want to
extend my sympathies of this and of this Council
to our local residents and staff who may have family
and friends impacted by the current war. I think it
was Mayor Liggett who reminded us last week of how
many global conflicts occur around the world at this very
moment. It is my hope that while conflicts rage globally,
that this community remains a place where all residents feel
safe and where the many aid organizations, NGOs, and Peace
Institutes located across our region can continue their work to
make a more peaceful global future. Today is also Persons
Day in Canada. Persons Day marks the day in 1929,
when courts struck down the law that defined persons as
men in Canada, excluding women from institutional institutions like the
Canadian Senate. This important appeal was won by Emily Murphy,
Nellie McClung, Irene Parlby, Louise McKinney, and Henrietta Muir Edwards,
also known as The Famous Five. many of you may
be familiar with the statue of the Famous Five in
Ottawa. Or if you're of a certain age, remember a
heritage moment that used to run on television. Today is
a reminder of the important role that individuals can play
in making a more equitable society and that these rights
are hard fought and not to be taken for granted.
